newsitem.title: UK: Diana sues paper for libel over ballgowns story.
newsitem.headline: Diana sues paper for libel over ballgowns story.

text.p: Diana, Princess of Wales, is to sue a British newspaper for libel over a story that claimed she would benefit from the sale of some of her evening gowns which are being auctioned for charity, her solicitor said on Monday.
Anthony Julius said in a statement that she was suing Richard Eddis, editor of the Express on Sunday, and Express Newspapers for the story which was published on Sunday.
"The Princess of Wales claims damages for the libel that, contrary to earlier press reports, she will benefit personally from the sale of a number of her dresses," the statement said.

Diana was divorced from heir to the throne Prince Charles last year. The ups and downs of her life as a royal were chronicled in detail by the press, but she has never before been moved to sue a newspaper for libel. She took action against Mirror Group Newspapers for the publication of photos taken of her exercising in her gym, but reached an out of court settlement on that occasion.

The sale of some of her designer gowns is expected to raise over one million pounds ($1.6 million) and her aides said all the money raised would go to two of her favourite charities, Aids Crisis Trust and the Royal Marsden Cancer Research Fund. REUTER AGR ($1=.6142 Pound)
